coarse_request: Please design an integrated business ecosystem process that includes the roles of 'university students', 'IT department', 'admissions office', 'gaming players', 'web design team', 'compliance auditors', and 'company'. The key activities are 'IT solutions implementation', 'university enrollment processing', 'farming bot operation', 'website development', and 'compliance auditing', and there should be decision points regarding 'IT request approval', 'application acceptance', 'game milestone achievements', 'website approval', and 'audit certification'.
fine_grained_text:
Step 1: The process starts when an employee or department submits a request for an IT solution, such as new software or hardware.
IT assesses the request, checking for compatibility with existing systems and evaluating cost and resource needs.
If approved, IT procures the necessary tools or licenses, installs the solution, and tests it in a controlled environment.
After successful testing, the new solution is rolled out to the requesting department.
Training may be provided, and IT support remains available for troubleshooting.
[Transition]: The implemented IT solutions from Process A provide the technological infrastructure and systems required for the university enrollment process in Process B, enabling online applications, student portals, email accounts, and grade review systems to function seamlessly.
Step 2: A university enrollment system involves the following steps:
Prospective students submit an application online.
The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes:
Meeting with an academic advisor.
Selecting courses.
Resolving any schedule conflicts.
The student begins attending classes.
Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes:
Submitting an appeal form.
Meeting with the appeals committee.
Awaiting a decision.
The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.
[Transition]: After completing the enrollment process and setting up their student accounts, users can log into the university’s digital portal to design and run the Farming Bot described in Process B, allowing them to gather virtual resources.
Step 3: Title: Farming Bot

Players want to create custom farming bots, that help them gather resources.
First you have to find out which resources you want.
Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes,  random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.
[Transition]: The successful operation and profit generation from the farming bot creates a business opportunity that necessitates a professional web presence, prompting the team to initiate the website development process to showcase and market the farming bot service to a broader audience.
Step 4: The process starts with an informational meeting among the web design team.
If this meeting is not successful, the process ends here.
Otherwise, the team starts by creating a storyboard.
After an agreement on the storyboard, part of the team starts working on the design and development of the website.
Simultaneously, the team will start to prepare an initial draft of the content.
In case a review of the draft is needed, the marketing team will conduct this, before the web design team creates the final version of the content.
When the development and content have been completed, the website will be built and reviewed.
If the site is approved, the process is completed, otherwise the team goes back to the building step.
[Transition]: Once the website receives final approval and the development process is completed, the company initiates a compliance audit to ensure the newly launched site meets regulatory standards such as ISO requirements, safety protocols, and environmental guidelines.
Step 5: The process starts when a company schedules a compliance audit for regulations such as ISO standards, safety protocols, or environmental guidelines.
Internal teams prepare documentation, gather evidence, and conduct a self-assessment before the external audit.
Auditors review the company's processes and identify any gaps or issues.
After making the necessary corrections or improvements, the company undergoes a final audit.
If all criteria are met, the company is awarded certification, and the process concludes with the issuance of official documents.
bridge_logics: The implemented IT solutions from Process A provide the technological infrastructure and systems required for the university enrollment process in Process B, enabling online applications, student portals, email accounts, and grade review systems to function seamlessly.

After completing the enrollment process and setting up their student accounts, users can log into the university’s digital portal to design and run the Farming Bot described in Process B, allowing them to gather virtual resources.

The successful operation and profit generation from the farming bot creates a business opportunity that necessitates a professional web presence, prompting the team to initiate the website development process to showcase and market the farming bot service to a broader audience.
